summaryZh: Coufal 实验室研究小胶质细胞功能障碍如何导致人类神经疾病，以及何时可将其作为治疗靶点。团队使用人干细胞来源模型、患者与 CRISPR 改造细胞系、脑类器官共培养和小鼠异种移植。

evidence.quote: COUFAL LAB RESEARCH PEOPLE PUBLICATIONS NEWS JOIN US! FUNDING RESOURCES Contact Coufal Lab ​ Microglia in Health & Disease Human microglia, although they represent only a small fraction of cells of the adult brain, are the predominant glial cell during much of human brain development. Surprisingly little is known about the microglial contribution to normal brain development, or how microglial dysfunction contributes to the pathogenesis or neurodevelopmental disorders. A major focus of our lab is understanding how microglial dysfunction contributes to human neurological disease and to determine in what contexts and situations microglia represent a novel therapeutic target. ​Through the application of human stem cell derived models of microglial biology, combining patient derived and CRISPR modified lines we strive to understand the molecular determinants of microglial fate, functionality, and signaling. To delineate the interaction of microglia with the developing brain and vice versa, we have helped generate and validate cerebral organoid cocultures and a murine xenotransplantation model. GOALS 1. Identify determinants of microglial environmental dependence and delineate signaling interactions with the developing brain 2. Uncover novel contributions and molecular mechanisms by which microglia contribute to the pathogenesis of pediatric neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders. 3. Identify novel therapeutic targets that can be validated through our models to ultimately treat currently untreatable pediatric neurological disorders. Twitter: @CoufalNicole @CoufalLab ​ Email: [email protected] LAB PHILOSOPHY The goal of the lab is to understand the role of microglia in neurodevelopment and their contribution to common and rare neurodevelopmental disorders. The philosophy of the lab is to promote teamwork, individual career development, and research excellence through support of one another. Every lab member brings something essential to the team and we achieve research excellence through collaborative approaches. RESEARCH PEOPLE PUBLICATIONS FUNDING NEWS Join us!
